title: Exemplar Brokering Scrapbook
content:
Purpose / fridge notes:
- Goal: build a lightweight "exemplar broker" service that picks (and optionally rewrites) a small set of exemplars for each query at request-time. Improve downstream accuracy and control token cost.
- Keep it simple to start: reranker + diversity heuristic + token budget enforcement.

High-level idea (sketch):
1) Candidate pool: precomputed exemplar bank per domain (training examples, curated prompts, community snippets). Metadata: domain tag, canonical length, embedding vector id, last-used timestamp, quality_score (eval), source (team/author).
2) For each incoming query:
   - quick signal gather: query embedding, length, explicit style tag (if present), token_budget (derived from route), risk_profile (safety), recency_bias (if user is in session).
   - rerank by combined score = alpha * sim(query, exemplar) + beta * exemplar_quality - gamma * length_penalty + delta * recency_boost + epsilon * diversity_penalty
   - diversity_penalty: discourage near-duplicate exemplars (embedding-sim > 0.92)
   - enforce token budget: greedily pick top-ranked until budget left < min_shot_margin. If budget too tight, fall back to templated zero-shot or 1-shot.

Quick failure modes to watch (observed in experiments):
- Anchor dominance: single strong exemplar distorts tone/assumptions (especially with longer exemplars).
- Hallucination amplification: exemplars containing factual errors increase hallucination risk if similarity weighting is too heavy.
- Style bleed: mixing exemplars from different registers causes inconsistent voice in answer.
- Token blowout: naive concatenation of exemplars + instructions exceeds prompt limit; we need progressive trimming and compressed exemplars (abbreviations).
- Latency cliff: reranking embeddings + fetching exemplars adds ~40-120ms; heavy on p95.

Experiment logs (very rough):
- run 2025-01-20: baseline static 3-shot (handpicked). Eval set: 400 queries. Metrics: exact-match 0.61, nlg-bleu-like 0.44, cost per request 1.0x, p95 latency 480ms.
- run 2025-01-27: brokering v0 (dense sim + quality score, no diversity). 3-shot on average. exact-match 0.66, nlg 0.46, hallucination rate +6% on factual retrieval tasks. Observed anchor dominance on 8% of cases.
- run 2025-02-10: brokering v1 (add diversity penalty + length penalty + token budget). exact-match 0.68, nlg 0.48, hallucination rate back to baseline. p95 latency +70ms.

Example exemplar templates (for developer-facing completion helpers):
- Template A (instruction-focused):
  "You are an assistant that translates developer intent into a short code comment. Examples:
  Q: "Write a test that ensures POST /login rejects bad creds"
  A: "Add an integration test that posts invalid credentials to /login and asserts 401 and error body"
  Q: "Summarize this PR"
  A: "Brief: refactor caching layer to use bulk invalidation; risk: cache stampede; test: add concurrency test"
  ===
  Now respond to:
  Q: {{USER_QUERY}}
  A:"

- Template B (few-shot dialog style, high brevity):
  "Example 1:
  User: How do I rotate keys in prod?
  Bot: 1) Create new key in KMS 2) Deploy config 3) Roll traffic 4) Depricate old key
  Example 2:
  User: What's a quick rollback plan?
  Bot: Keep hot backups, versioned images, immediate routing change via LB
  ===
  User: {{USER_QUERY}}
  Bot:"

Small curated few-shot set (for security-guidance domain) — keep these concise to avoid anchor dominance:
- Shot 1: Q: "How to securely store API tokens in a web app?" A: "Use dedicated secrets manager, env vars at runtime, rotate regularly, never check into VCS."
- Shot 2: Q: "What to do on key compromise?" A: "Revoke, rotate, audit logs, notify stakeholders, rotate downstream credentials."
- Shot 3: Q: "Minimum RBAC for internal tooling?" A: "Least privilege + short-lived sessions + audit trails."

Selection heuristics to test (abbrev):
- Signal set: [embedding_sim, exemplar_length_tokens, exemplar_quality_score, last_used_days, source_trust_level]
- Score mixing strategies: linear combo, learned logistic weight, simple rules (if sim>0.9 and quality>0.8 then prefer 1-shot).

Microbench checklist (what to instrument):
- token_cost_delta (selected_exemplars) vs baseline_template
- per-route p50/p95 latency impact from brokering service
- failure buckets annotated by human raters: {tone_mismatch, hallucination_add, inaccurate_example_copying, response_fragmentation}
- exemplar reuse heatmap (which exemplars get used how often)

Operational ideas / cheap wins:
- store compressed exemplar digest (2–3 sentence paraphrase) and prefer those when budget small
- auto-generate a "micro-exemplar" by extracting 1–2 key lines from long examples (reduce anchor power)
- periodic smoke checks: sample queries to ensure exemplars don't drift (quality_score monotonic)
- blacklist exemplars by source if they show repeated factual errors

Open questions / next experiments:
- How much learned mixing helps vs tuned linear combo? (A/B test: holdout queries, measure delta on QA and hallucination)
- Should we expose exemplar provenance to customers? (privacy + leakage risk)
- Best representation for diversity penalty: embedding distance threshold vs maximal marginal relevance (MMR) style scoring?
- How to do realtime exemplar rewriting safely? (compression + sanitize PII + canonicalize style)

Quick TODOs (near term):
- [ ] Build small reranker lambda + index (Arjun) - prototype end-to-end with 5k exemplars (due 2025-02-05)
- [ ] Add token_budget enforcement in the prompt builder (Maya) - include micro-exemplar fallback (due 2025-02-12)
- [ ] Human eval rubric for anchor dominance and hallucination; run on 500 random samples (Sofia) - start 2025-02-20
- [ ] Add instrumentation (cost delta, p95 impact, exemplar reuse) in Redwood Console route (Benji)

Notes to self: keep good experiment names, log seed for reranker stochastics, and snapshot exemplar bank each major change. This file is messy — intended to be a rolling notebook for design + quick examples.

References + quick links:

- Slack thread: #prompt-infra (see thread around Jan 24th)

End of scrapbook.
